name: hashtagweb3.com
ctaMessage: You're ahead of most. Here's where you're still exposed.
agenticSummary: Hashtagweb3 offers strong access control, and developer resource discoverability would improve agent support.

checks.name: ARD discovery
checks.details: ARD catalog valid at /.well-known/ard.json (spec 0.91) - 4/4 entries, trustManifest present
checks.recommendation: Publish an Agentic Resource Discovery catalog at /.well-known/ard.json (the ARD v0.91 canonical path; the legacy /.well-known/ai-catalog.json remains a valid alias) listing your agentic resources (MCP servers, agents, skills, APIs), each entry with a urn:air identifier, a media type, and exactly one of url or data. See https://agenticresourcediscovery.org/

checks.name: AI Catalog discovery
checks.details: Valid AI Catalog at /.well-known/ai-catalog.json (spec 0.91) - 4/4 entries
checks.recommendation: Serve a valid catalog at /.well-known/ai-catalog.json - the AI Catalog Standard's own discovery path - so consumers following that spec (see https://ai-catalog.io/) also find you. The same document you serve at /.well-known/ard.json works unchanged.

checks.name: ARD entry validity
checks.details: All 4 entries valid with domain-anchored urn:air identifiers (catalog at /.well-known/ard.json)
checks.recommendation: Make every catalog entry fully valid: a domain-anchored urn:air identifier, a displayName, a media type, and exactly one of url or data. Applies to the catalog at /.well-known/ard.json or the legacy /.well-known/ai-catalog.json.

checks.name: ARD trust manifest
checks.details: trustManifest present on catalog entries (4/4 entries valid, catalog at /.well-known/ard.json)
checks.recommendation: Add a trustManifest (verifiable identity, compliance attestations, or signature) to your catalog entries (ard.json, or the legacy ai-catalog.json) so clients can verify your resources with progressive trust.

checks.name: Category share of voice
checks.details: Category share of voice is in beta. It measures whether agents surface you for capability and use-case searches (not just your name). We are tuning it for accuracy before it counts toward your score - coming soon as a Pro check.
checks.recommendation: Build topical authority for your category. Publish comparison pages, 'best X for Y' content, tutorials, and integration guides that rank for generic use-case queries - not just your brand name - so agents surface you when users describe a need.

checks.name: Developer resource discoverability
checks.details: Agent struggled to find developer resources by name - only 1 result(s) out of 9
checks.recommendation: Make your developer resources (API docs, OpenAPI spec, auth docs, developer portal, MCP server) discoverable by name. Publish them at predictable URLs, list them in llms.txt, and include your product name in page titles and headings so search engines surface them for name-based queries.

checks.name: Brand name discoverability
checks.details: hashtagweb3.com appears at position #2 in a clean brand-name search for "Hashtag Web3" (1 total match)
checks.recommendation: Make sure a clean search for your brand name returns your own domain in the top results. If it does not, your brand may be too generic, conflict with a more established term, or not yet indexed. Strengthen brand-name search by claiming consistent NAP across listings, earning press mentions that link to the canonical domain, and avoiding redirect chains that mask the apex domain in search results.

checks.name: Wikipedia / Wikidata entity presence
checks.details: No Wikipedia article or Wikidata entity found for "hashtagweb3" - creating a Wikipedia page and a Wikidata item with P856 = hashtagweb3.com is the highest-impact step for AI search citation coverage
checks.recommendation: Establish a Wikipedia article and a Wikidata entity for your brand, with the domain set as the official website (Wikidata property P856) and a corresponding external link on Wikipedia. Wikipedia is the largest single source of citations in ChatGPT and a primary input to Knowledge Graphs across Google, Bing, and LLM training data. Earn third-party press coverage first to satisfy notability, then draft the article with cited references rather than self-promotion.

checks.name: robots.txt AI crawler policy
checks.details: Tier-aware Content Signals policy (search=yes, ai-train=no) - search allowed, ai-train blocked
checks.recommendation: Add explicit AI crawler directives in robots.txt. Allow the crawlers that feed answer engines ('User-agent: GPTBot' / 'Allow: /', same for ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, OAI-SearchBot), and restrict training-only crawlers (CCBot, ByteSpider) with 'Disallow: /'. Content Signals ('Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-train=no') earns the same credit.

checks.name: Listed in MCP registries
checks.details: No bi-directionally verified MCP registry entry found. To pass, either publish the server under your own domain/npm scope, get a verified Smithery listing with non-zero usage, or link the registry entry from your homepage or docs.
checks.recommendation: Register your MCP server on Smithery (smithery.ai) or mcp.so so agent platforms can discover your tools. Link the registry entry from your homepage or docs for bi-directional verification.

checks.name: NPM/PyPI SDK package
checks.details: No NPM or PyPI SDK package found
checks.recommendation: Publish a JavaScript/TypeScript SDK package on npm so developers can integrate your API programmatically. In package.json set `repository` to your source repo and `homepage` to your product domain - these links are how agents confirm the package is your official SDK rather than a third-party tool with a similar name.

checks.name: Agent platform configs
checks.details: Could not locate a public repo containing agent configs or rules. If our probes missed it, AI coding agents likely will too - link the repo from your homepage or docs so it's discoverable.
checks.recommendation: Add an AGENTS.md or .cursorrules file to your public GitHub repo with instructions for how AI coding agents should interact with your codebase. Then make sure the repo is documented in the entry-point pages agents read - homepage, docs, and llms.txt - so it can be discovered without guessing.

checks.name: Agent Plugins manifest
checks.details: No Agent Plugins manifest (plugin.json) found in discovered repos
checks.recommendation: Bundle your agent skills and MCP servers as an Agent Plugin: add a plugin.json manifest with the agent-plugins.org $schema and a name. See https://agent-plugins.org/specification

checks.name: Listed on skills.sh
checks.details: No official skills self-published on skills.sh (1 community skill with potential relation to this domain found, but only self-published official skills count)
checks.recommendation: Publish agent skills on skills.sh so AI agents can discover your product's capabilities. Create a SKILL.md in your GitHub repo and register it with 'npx skills add'. See skills.sh/docs.

checks.name: Registry branding
checks.details: MCP manifest has full branding (name, icon, description) at /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json
checks.recommendation: Give your MCP server-card (at /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json) a display name, an icon or logo, and a description - all three together are what reads as a complete, branded listing agents can present.

checks.name: ChatGPT app listed
checks.details: ChatGPT plugin manifest found: "Hashtag Web3"
checks.recommendation: Submit your app to the ChatGPT apps / connectors directory (the apps-in-ChatGPT surface) so ChatGPT users can discover and use your product.

checks.name: Sitemap exists
checks.details: Valid sitemap found at https://hashtagweb3.com/sitemap.xml with 3074 entries
checks.recommendation: Add a valid XML sitemap at /sitemap.xml listing all indexable URLs. Include lastmod dates and keep it under 50MB.

checks.name: Content without JavaScript
checks.details: 5375 chars, semantic headings (1 H1 + 5 H2s + 62 H3s), 8.3% content ratio
checks.recommendation: Serve at least 500 characters of meaningful homepage content in raw HTML. Add a clear H1, keep deeper heading levels sequential, and remove excessive non-content markup.

checks.name: Not blocked by bot detection
checks.details: Site accessible to 6 AI agent user-agents
checks.recommendation: Allowlist known AI agent User-Agents (ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, DeepSeekBot) in your WAF or bot-detection rules.

checks.name: Agent discovery file
checks.details: Agent Skills index (agentskills.io) found at /.well-known/agent-skills/index.json with 5 skill(s)
checks.recommendation: Publish an Agent Skills index at /.well-known/agent-skills/index.json that lists your capabilities, with each skill carrying a name and a description so agents can find and parse what you offer.

checks.name: Agent Skills index conformance (v0.2.0)
checks.details: Index v0.2.0 conformant; verified SHA-256 of "search_jobs" (4 other skills present)
checks.recommendation: Upgrade /.well-known/agent-skills/index.json to the v0.2.0 schema: add "$schema": "https://schemas.agentskills.io/discovery/0.2.0/schema.json", and give every entry a type (skill-md or archive), url, and digest. Use "digest": "sha256:<64 lowercase hex chars>" (e.g. "digest": "sha256:a3f1...") - a bare "sha256": "<hex>" field is also accepted. Compute the value from the artifact's raw bytes.

checks.name: A2A / agent-card
checks.details: A2A Agent Card found: "Hashtag Web3 Agent"
checks.recommendation: Publish an Agent-to-Agent (A2A) agent card at /.well-known/agent-card.json describing your agent's capabilities, skills, and contact endpoint.

checks.name: pricing.md exists
checks.details: No pricing.md found - agents need machine-readable pricing to compare products and make purchase recommendations
checks.recommendation: Create a /pricing.md file with your pricing tiers, features, and limits in plain markdown. This lets AI agents compare costs and recommend plans without scraping HTML pricing pages.
checks.naReason: no paid surface; product is free, so machine-readable pricing does not apply

checks.name: NLWeb Schema Feeds
checks.details: Valid Schema Map XML found at https://hashtagweb3.com/schemamap.xml
checks.recommendation: Add a schemamap: directive to robots.txt pointing to a Schema Map XML file listing your structured data feeds (JSONL/RSS). See the NLWeb Schema Feeds spec.

checks.name: MCP well-known discovery
checks.details: MCP server discoverable at standard path https://hashtagweb3.com/.well-known/mcp.json
checks.recommendation: Serve your MCP server at /.well-known/mcp, publish a server-card.json at /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json, or reference it in llms.txt so agents can discover it automatically without manual URL input.

checks.name: Agent mode view
checks.details: Agent mode view found at ?mode=agent (6 signals: llms.txt, openapi, mcp, api, endpoint, agent)
checks.recommendation: Add a ?mode=agent query parameter to your homepage that returns a structured, machine-readable view with API endpoints, authentication info, and key capabilities instead of marketing HTML.

checks.name: HTTP Link headers (RFC 8288)
checks.details: RFC 8288 Link header advertises: sitemap, service-desc, api-catalog
checks.recommendation: Add HTTP Link: response headers (RFC 8288) advertising your sitemap, markdown alternates, API service descriptions, and API catalog. Example: Link: </sitemap.xml>; rel="sitemap", </index.md>; rel="alternate"; type="text/markdown".

checks.name: Markdown URL fallback
checks.details: Full markdown fallback support. Homepage (https://hashtagweb3.com/index.md) and all 3 sampled content pages return markdown: https://hashtagweb3.com/.well-known/api-catalog.md, https://hashtagweb3.com/.well-known/mcp-docs/server-card.json.md, https://hashtagweb3.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.md
checks.recommendation: Let agents fetch markdown by appending .md to page URLs. Required for any credit: serve a markdown homepage at /index.md. For full credit (2/2): also serve a .md twin for each content page (e.g. /docs/auth -> /docs/auth.md). Content-Type should be text/markdown and the body should start with a top-level heading (not HTML).

checks.name: Modular llms.txt per product area
checks.details: Modular llms.txt files found for sections: docs, api, developers
checks.recommendation: Add per-section llms.txt files (e.g. /docs/llms.txt, /api/llms.txt, /developers/llms.txt) so agents can fetch scoped context for specific product areas instead of the whole manual.

checks.name: Sitemap freshness (lastmod)
checks.details: 100% of 500 sampled sitemap entries carry lastmod; newest is 0 day(s) old
checks.recommendation: Add <lastmod> dates (W3C datetime, e.g. 2026-08-01) to your sitemap entries and update them when content actually changes. Aim for lastmod on at least half your entries with the newest within the last year. Verify with `curl https://yourdomain.com/sitemap.xml | grep lastmod`.

checks.name: robots.txt agent-user policy
checks.details: User-triggered agents explicitly allowed (chatgpt-user)
checks.recommendation: Stop blocking user-triggered agents in robots.txt. Remove any 'Disallow: /' that applies to ChatGPT-User, Claude-User or Perplexity-User - including a blanket 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /', which covers them by default. These agents fetch a page only because a person just asked about you, so a block turns away your highest-intent traffic.

checks.name: llms.txt exists
checks.details: Found the llms.txt at https://hashtagweb3.com/llms.txt.
checks.recommendation: Create an llms.txt file at your domain root (/llms.txt) - the AI equivalent of robots.txt. Write at least 100 characters of real content: what your product is, what it does, and links to your key docs. Then verify it with `curl https://yourdomain.com/llms.txt` - you should see your text, not HTML. If your app returns its homepage for every URL (common with single-page apps), add a static file route so the raw text is served. A placeholder with just a heading earns no credit.

checks.name: llms.txt formatting
checks.details: The llms.txt is well-formatted: 143 lines with markdown links, 13,828 characters in total.
checks.recommendation: Format your llms.txt as a navigation index: start with a markdown heading, include markdown links to deeper resources, and keep it under 30,000 characters. If you have more to say, move long-form content into /llms-full.txt or per-section files (e.g. /docs/llms.txt, /api/llms.txt) and link to them from the main index.

checks.name: JSON-LD structured data
checks.details: Rich JSON-LD identity: Organization with name, description, url, and sameAs/logo/address (6 block(s))
checks.recommendation: Add JSON-LD structured data to your homepage using the identity type that matches your site - SoftwareApplication for products, Organization or LocalBusiness for companies, Person for personal sites, Article for blogs - with name, description, url, and type-appropriate fields (offers, sameAs, author) so AI can parse your identity programmatically.

checks.name: Pricing info accessible
checks.details: Pricing page found at /plans
checks.recommendation: Make pricing discoverable - add a /pricing page or include pricing as schema.org/Offer structured data, so agents can find it without scraping a marketing page.

checks.name: Public API/docs linked from homepage
checks.details: Documentation found at /docs but not linked from homepage
checks.recommendation: Publish API documentation at a discoverable URL (/docs, /api, /developers). Include authentication, endpoints, and example requests.

checks.name: Agent instruction / when-to-use
checks.details: Agent instruction file at /.well-known/agents.json but no explicit when-to-use guidance
checks.recommendation: Tell agents when to reach for you: add a 'when to use this' section to your llms.txt (or a dedicated agent-instructions file) that names your best-fit use cases and how an agent should call you. Be specific about the jobs you are right for - generic marketing copy does not read as guidance.

checks.name: Skills.sh skill quality
checks.details: No official skills on skills.sh to evaluate
checks.recommendation: Expand your skills.sh presence with multiple skill repos covering different use cases. Add descriptive skill names, clear SKILL.md files, and organize by capability area.

checks.name: JSON-LD entity linking (sameAs)
checks.details: Strong entity linking via sameAs: linkedin.com, github.com
checks.recommendation: Add sameAs links in your JSON-LD structured data pointing to your Wikipedia page, Wikidata entry, GitHub org, and social profiles. This helps AI disambiguate your brand from similarly named entities.

checks.name: Metadata completeness
checks.details: All metadata signals present: canonical URL, lang="en", og:image, og:type
checks.recommendation: Add all four signals to your homepage: <link rel="canonical">, <html lang="...">, <meta property="og:image">, and <meta property="og:type">. Agents use these for entity resolution and attribution.

checks.name: Organization schema completeness
checks.details: Organization schema complete with contactPoint and address
checks.recommendation: Add Organization JSON-LD that includes both contactPoint (with email/phone and contactType) and address (PostalAddress). This lets AI verify your business legitimacy and answer contact queries.

checks.name: Schema type breadth
checks.details: Rich schema vocabulary: ItemList, Service, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList
checks.recommendation: Expand your JSON-LD beyond Organization/WebSite. Add FAQPage for common questions, Service or Product for offerings, AggregateRating or Review for social proof, and BreadcrumbList for navigation context.

checks.name: Trust anchor pages
checks.details: All trust anchor pages verified: About, Contact, Privacy
checks.recommendation: Publish real /about, /contact, and /privacy pages with at least 500 characters of content each. These are the pages AI agents check to verify your business is legitimate before recommending you.

checks.name: llms.txt links resolve
checks.details: All 5 probed llms.txt links resolve to real content
checks.recommendation: Make every link your llms.txt declares resolve to real content. Verify each one with `curl -L <url>` - you should see the linked document, not your homepage. If your app returns the homepage shell for unknown paths (common with single-page apps), a 200 status is not proof: check the body. Fix or remove any dead link; agents that follow the index treat a broken link as a dead end.

checks.name: Markdown alternate link
checks.details: Markdown alternate advertised and verified: https://hashtagweb3.com/index.md serves markdown
checks.recommendation: Advertise a markdown twin of each page with <link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown" href="..."> in the HTML head (or an equivalent Link response header), and make sure the advertised URL actually serves markdown - an advertisement pointing at HTML is worse than none. Verify the target with `curl -s <href>` and check the body starts with a heading, not <!doctype html>.

checks.name: Markdown frontmatter metadata
checks.details: Frontmatter with title + description, canonical, and last-updated on /index.md
checks.recommendation: Open your served markdown docs with a --- frontmatter block carrying title plus at least one of description, canonical, or last-updated. Agents read frontmatter as document metadata without scraping. A Link: rel="canonical" response header also satisfies the canonical slot.

checks.name: Redirect hygiene
checks.details: No meta-refresh stubs, JavaScript-redirect stubs, or cross-domain hops across 6 checked pages
checks.recommendation: Replace meta-refresh and JavaScript-only redirects with real HTTP 301/302 redirects. Non-JS agents never execute `location.href` or wait for a meta refresh - they see only the stub page. Verify with `curl -sI <url>` - you should see a Location header, not a 200 with a near-empty body.

checks.name: Page token budget
checks.details: All 8 measured pages fit an agent context budget (largest ~1K tokens)
checks.recommendation: Keep each page's extracted text under ~100K characters (~25K tokens) so it fits an agent's context window without truncation. Split oversized reference pages into focused per-topic documents and link them from an index. Check a page with `curl -s <url> | wc -c` and remember agents read the extracted text, not the raw HTML.

checks.name: Code fence validity
checks.details: Code fences balanced across 2 markdown documents
checks.recommendation: Close every fenced code block (``` or ~~~) in your served markdown. CommonMark treats everything after an unclosed fence as code, so an agent parsing the document silently loses the rest of it. Count fence lines per file - the total must be even.

checks.name: Content behind auth
checks.details: All 5 sampled pages are publicly readable (5 with substantive content)
checks.recommendation: Serve your content pages without a login wall. Agents cannot complete auth flows while browsing - a 401/403 or a login-form page is invisible content. Keep public documentation public; if some content must stay gated, publish an ungated summary so agents can still represent it.

checks.name: OpenAPI spec published
checks.details: OpenAPI spec found at https://hashtagweb3.com/openapi.json (version: 3.1.0)
checks.recommendation: Publish an OpenAPI (Swagger) specification at /openapi.json or /api/openapi.yaml. This is how agents understand your API surface automatically.

checks.name: Developer portal
checks.details: Developer portal found at /developers
checks.recommendation: Create a developer portal at /developers with API keys, documentation, quickstart guides, and a sandbox environment.

checks.name: API catalog (RFC 9727)
checks.details: RFC 9727 api-catalog with 7 API link(s) and rfc9727 profile
checks.recommendation: Publish an API catalog at /.well-known/api-catalog per RFC 9727. Serve it with Content-Type: application/linkset+json;profile="https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9727" and include a 'linkset' array with item entries pointing to your OpenAPI specs and service descriptions.

checks.name: Markdown agent docs
checks.details: Path-suffix markdown docs served with text/markdown content-type: /auth.md, /index.md
checks.recommendation: Pick one: (a) return Content-Type: text/markdown on GET <homepage> when the request sends Accept: text/markdown, or (b) publish a static /llms.md, /auth.md, or /agents.md file at your root with real markdown content. Option (b) is usually a single static file. This is the cold-discovery path for agents that land at your homepage from web search without reading llms.txt first.

checks.name: Markdown content negotiation (acceptmarkdown.com)
checks.details: Canonical URL serves text/markdown and text/html via Accept negotiation with Vary: Accept
checks.recommendation: On the responses that serve text/markdown via Accept negotiation, add Accept to the Vary header (Vary: Accept, Accept-Encoding). Without it, CDNs can serve the cached HTML variant to an agent asking for markdown (or vice versa), depending on which variant landed in cache first.

checks.name: Bot-UA markdown serving
checks.details: No probed bot User-Agent (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended, ora-agent, DeepSeekBot) receives markdown when requesting HTML. Optional: detect AI-bot UAs server-side and serve them a markdown representation directly.
checks.recommendation: Optionally detect AI-bot User-Agents (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot) server-side and serve them a markdown representation of the page directly, even when they send Accept: text/html. Verify with `curl -A "ClaudeBot/1.0" https://yourdomain.com/` - a markdown body earns this bonus. Accept-header negotiation is scored separately.

checks.name: Agent crawler reachability
checks.details: Reachable to all major AI crawlers - ChatGPT-User: reachable, ClaudeBot: reachable, Google-Extended: reachable, ora-agent: reachable, DeepSeekBot: reachable
checks.recommendation: Allowlist the major AI crawler/agent User-Agents (ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, ora-agent, DeepSeekBot) in your WAF, bot-detection rules, and robots.txt so agents can reach your homepage.

checks.name: MCP tool descriptions
checks.details: All 4 tools on docs MCP have detailed descriptions (>= 30 chars)
checks.recommendation: Add detailed descriptions (>= 20 chars) to every MCP tool. Agents use these to decide which tool to call - vague descriptions lead to wrong tool selection.

checks.name: MCP parameter schemas
checks.details: 4/4 tools on docs MCP have parameter schemas
checks.recommendation: Define inputSchema with typed properties and required arrays for each tool. Agents need schema info to construct valid tool calls without guessing.

checks.name: MCP server identity
checks.details: docs MCP identifies as "hashtagweb3-product-mcp" v1.0.0 with instructions
checks.recommendation: Set server name, version, and instructions in your MCP server's initialize response. Instructions help agents understand your server's purpose and constraints.

checks.name: MCP tool listing
checks.details: docs MCP exposes 4 tools - consider consolidating to keep agent attention focused on retrieval
checks.recommendation: Expose 3+ tools via your MCP server's tools/list endpoint. Cover your core API surface - agents need tools for read, write, and search operations.

checks.name: MCP tool naming
checks.details: All 4 tool names follow consistent convention, descriptive, and non-generic
checks.recommendation: Use consistent naming conventions (snake_case or camelCase) for all MCP tools. Names should be descriptive (>= 4 chars) and not generic (avoid 'run', 'get', 'do').

checks.name: Public API with reachable endpoints
checks.details: REST API documentation found at https://hashtagweb3.com/developers. Best-of-protocols score: 7/7.
checks.recommendation: Expose a public REST or GraphQL API. AI agents need programmatic access  - not just a web UI  - to integrate with your product.

checks.name: OAuth 2.0 support
checks.details: OAuth authorization server metadata at https://hashtagweb3.com (issuer=https://hashtagweb3.com)
checks.recommendation: Implement OAuth 2.0 for API authentication. Publish your authorization server metadata at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.

checks.name: Scoped permissions
checks.details: scopes_supported declares 4 scope(s) in RFC 9728 metadata (e.g. read:jobs, read:news, read:events)
checks.recommendation: Declare scoped API permissions where machines can read them: named OAuth scopes in your OpenAPI security schemes, or scopes_supported in RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata. Prose descriptions of roles help humans, but agents need the machine-readable declaration to request least-privilege access.

checks.name: MCP auth mechanism
checks.details: docs MCP is public - correct posture for documentation surface
checks.recommendation: Protect your MCP server with OAuth 2.0 authentication. Publish authorization server metadata at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server for automatic agent auth flows.

checks.name: MCP OAuth metadata
checks.details: docs MCP has authentication disabled - OAuth metadata not applicable
checks.recommendation: Publish RFC 8414 authorization server metadata with issuer, authorization_endpoint, and token_endpoint so agents can authenticate without hardcoded URLs. For client registration, advertise client_id_metadata_document_supported (CIMD) - Dynamic Client Registration is deprecated and worth keeping only as a compatibility path.

checks.name: MCP PKCE S256 support
checks.details: docs MCP has authentication disabled - PKCE not applicable
checks.recommendation: Support PKCE with S256 code challenge method in your OAuth server. Add 'S256' to code_challenge_methods_supported in your authorization server metadata.

checks.name: Agent onboarding friction
checks.details: Zero-friction onboarding verified live: keyless API surface fetched without credentials - no signup step exists
checks.recommendation: Offer a free tier or trial, self-serve API key generation, and a sandbox environment. Agents can't fill out 'contact sales' forms.

checks.name: Web Bot Auth directory
checks.details: Web Bot Auth directory with 1 Ed25519 key(s), all with kid + nbf/exp
checks.recommendation: Publish a Web Bot Auth directory at /.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory. Serve a JSON document with a 'keys' array of Ed25519 JWKs (kty=OKP, crv=Ed25519, kid, nbf, exp). This lets agents sign their requests per RFC 9421 so you can distinguish legitimate bots from spoofers.

checks.name: OAuth Protected Resource metadata (RFC 9728)
checks.details: RFC 9728 metadata: resource=https://hashtagweb3.com/api, authorization_servers (1), scopes_supported (4), bearer_methods_supported
checks.recommendation: Publish RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource. Include the resource field plus enough supporting metadata - your authorization servers, supported scopes, accepted bearer methods - that an agent can work out how to authenticate without first triggering a 401.

checks.name: auth.md exists
checks.details: auth.md at https://hashtagweb3.com/auth.md served as text/markdown; charset=utf-8 (5000 chars)
checks.recommendation: Publish /auth.md as a markdown prose walkthrough of how agents should obtain credentials. Serve it with Content-Type: text/markdown, lead with a top-level heading, and write at least ~200 chars of real content (not just a placeholder). See the WorkOS auth.md spec at https://github.com/workos/auth.md.

checks.name: auth.md structure
checks.details: WorkOS auth.md structure at https://hashtagweb3.com/auth.md - 7/8 walkthrough sections (found Discover, Pick a method, Register, Claim, Use credential, Errors, and Revocation); anchors: oauth-protected-resource, oauth-authorization-server, and agent_auth; register shapes: id-jag shape
checks.recommendation: Structure /auth.md as the WorkOS spec prescribes: sections for Discover, Pick a method, Register, Claim, Exchange, Use the access_token, Errors, and Revocation, with spec anchor keywords (agent_auth, identity_endpoint, identity_assertion, service_auth, id-jag, WWW-Authenticate). Reference https://github.com/workos/auth.md.

checks.name: auth.md walkthrough simulation
checks.details: Static fallback (deep check disabled): PRM + AS metadata both reachable with agent_auth.identity_endpoint (https://hashtagweb3.com/api/auth/register) (advertised under the pre-v0.2 register_uri key); walkthrough discoverable end-to-end
checks.recommendation: Make your published auth-discovery chain traversable end to end: an agent starting at /auth.md (or your protected-resource metadata) should be able to follow the links to your authorization-server metadata and registration endpoint without hitting a dead link. Test the whole path, not just each file in isolation.

checks.name: Agent auth discovery metadata
checks.details: PRM + AS metadata cross-linked; agent_auth has identity_endpoint (https://hashtagweb3.com/api/auth/register) (advertised under the pre-v0.2 register_uri key), identity_types_supported [anonymous, identity_assertion] with the required per-type blocks, and skill -> https://hashtagweb3.com/auth.md (also advertised: claim_endpoint, events_endpoint; events_supported absent)
checks.recommendation: Publish RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource on your resource server (the host that actually serves the API, e.g. api.<apex>) with `resource` and `authorization_servers`. Publish RFC 8414 authorization-server metadata at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server on the AS origin, and include the WorkOS auth.md `agent_auth` block with `identity_endpoint`, `identity_types_supported` drawn from the spec enum (`anonymous`, `identity_assertion`, `service_auth` - the assertion variant, the ID-JAG URN `urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id-jag`, belongs inside `identity_assertion.assertion_types_supported`, not at the top level), and the `identity_assertion.assertion_types_supported` block when you advertise that type, so agents can check their assertion shape is accepted before minting. Cross-link by listing the AS origin in PRM `authorization_servers`, and point `agent_auth.skill` back at your published /auth.md. Spec: https://github.com/workos/auth.md.

checks.name: Agent auth WWW-Authenticate hint
checks.details: 401 at /api with spec-shaped WWW-Authenticate hint: Bearer resource_metadata="https://hashtagweb3.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"
checks.recommendation: Return a 401 carrying a spec-shaped `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="<your protected-resource metadata URL>"` header on your API's primary entry points, so an agent learns your auth requirements from one request instead of hunting for the well-known document. Point the metadata URL at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource on the host that serves the API. Spec: https://github.com/workos/auth.md.

checks.name: agent_auth endpoints reachable
checks.details: agent_auth endpoints reachable (source: AS metadata agent_auth block) - identity_endpoint: HTTP 200, claim_endpoint: HTTP 200, events_endpoint: HTTP 200
checks.recommendation: Make sure the URIs you advertise (in the AS metadata agent_auth block OR in your /auth.md prose) for identity_endpoint, claim_endpoint, and events_endpoint actually resolve. An OPTIONS preflight should return any HTTP status (2xx/3xx/4xx that isn't 404). DNS-level failure or a 404 means the discovery block / prose is stale - either remove the URI or stand up the endpoint.

checks.name: MCP server / manifest
checks.details: MCP server connected via Streamable HTTP - hashtagweb3-product-mcp v1.0.0 (protocol 2025-11-25)
checks.recommendation: Build an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server exposing your API as tools. Use Streamable HTTP transport for full score. This lets Claude, ChatGPT, and other AI agents call your product natively.

checks.name: MCP error handling
checks.details: docs MCP returns structured JSON-RPC errors with code and message
checks.recommendation: Return structured JSON-RPC errors (with code and message) when agents call invalid tools or pass bad arguments. Don't crash or return empty responses.

checks.name: MCP modern transport
checks.details: docs MCP uses modern Streamable HTTP transport
checks.recommendation: Upgrade your MCP server from legacy SSE to Streamable HTTP transport. HTTP+SSE is formally deprecated with a year-long offramp; Streamable HTTP is the current standard and supports bidirectional communication.

checks.name: WebMCP support
checks.details: Runtime-verified: 3 tools captured in a real browser session
checks.recommendation: Expose in-page tools via WebMCP, the W3C draft standard for browser-resident AI agents. Add toolname and tooldescription attributes to your action forms - they survive into server-rendered HTML, so scanners and agents can see them - and register richer tools from client-side JS with document.modelContext.registerTool() (navigator.modelContext is the deprecated pre-Chrome-150 alias). Chrome ships WebMCP in 157 after the 149-156 origin trial, and the ChatGPT desktop browser and ChatGPT Sites call WebMCP site tools since August 2026.

checks.name: Rate limit response headers
checks.details: The live API at https://hashtagweb3.com/api returns IETF RateLimit-* headers: ratelimit-limit, ratelimit-policy.
checks.recommendation: Return standard rate-limit headers on your API responses (the RFC RateLimit headers, plus Retry-After on a 429) so agents can self-throttle in real time, and document the conventions alongside your API.

checks.name: Idempotency-Key support
checks.details: REST Idempotency-Key header found on POST /api/jobs/export in OpenAPI spec
checks.recommendation: Support an idempotency key on your write operations and declare it where agents can read it: an Idempotency-Key header parameter on your POST/PUT/PATCH operations in your OpenAPI spec for REST, or a client-supplied id argument on your GraphQL mutations. Agents retry on network failures, and without this a retry can double-charge or duplicate a record.

checks.name: JSON error responses
checks.details: API returns JSON error responses (404 at https://hashtagweb3.com/api/v1 (from OpenAPI servers))
checks.recommendation: Return structured JSON error responses with error codes, messages, and resolution hints. Agents can't parse HTML error pages.

checks.name: REST typed error model
checks.details: OpenAPI defines a typed error schema in components.schemas and 4xx/5xx responses reference it
checks.recommendation: Document your error responses in your OpenAPI spec: give 4xx and 5xx responses a typed error schema (or use RFC 9457 application/problem+json). A consistent error object with a machine-readable code and a human-readable message lets agents handle failures without guessing.

checks.name: REST versioning / deprecation policy
checks.details: API versioning strategy found (URL versioning) with deprecation policy documented at https://hashtagweb3.com/api-policy
checks.recommendation: Declare a versioning policy agents can rely on: version your API (in the URL path or a version header) and publish how you signal deprecation (a Sunset/Deprecation header or a documented timeline). Agents avoid integrating against a surface that can change without warning.

checks.name: REST pagination pattern
checks.details: Cursor-based pagination found in OpenAPI spec response schemas or query parameters
checks.recommendation: Use a consistent, documented pagination shape on your list endpoints (cursor-based preferred) and define the pagination fields in your OpenAPI response schemas, so agents can page through results without guessing the shape.

checks.name: REST async-job pattern
checks.details: Async job pattern detected: 202 Accepted with a Location header or job-tracking fields on the 202 body
checks.recommendation: For long-running operations, return 202 Accepted and point agents at where to poll for the result (a status/location reference plus a job identifier in the body), documented in your OpenAPI spec, so work that does not finish in one request is still followable.

checks.name: CLI tool available
checks.details: CLI tool mentioned at https://hashtagweb3.com/developers/llms.txt
checks.recommendation: Publish an official CLI tool on npm, PyPI, or Homebrew. A CLI lets agents and developers script interactions with your product without building API integrations from scratch.

checks.name: Multi-language SDK packages
checks.details: SDK packages mentioned at https://hashtagweb3.com/developers/llms.txt but none found in registries
checks.recommendation: Publish official SDK packages across multiple language ecosystems (npm, PyPI, Go modules, RubyGems). Auto-generate them from your OpenAPI spec using tools like openapi-generator. For each package set the project URL or homepage to your product domain (package.json `repository`/`homepage`, PyPI `Home-Page` or `project_urls`, RubyGems `homepage_uri`) - this is how agents verify the package is your official SDK.

checks.name: NLWeb /ask endpoint
checks.details: NLWeb /ask endpoint returns JSON with _meta (partial conformance, via GET)
checks.recommendation: Implement Microsoft's NLWeb protocol by adding a POST /ask endpoint that accepts natural-language queries and returns JSON with _meta (response_type, version). See github.com/microsoft/NLWeb.

checks.name: NLWeb streaming support
checks.details: NLWeb /ask supports SSE streaming with valid event data (via GET)
checks.recommendation: Add SSE streaming to your NLWeb /ask endpoint. Accept prefer.streaming: true and respond with Content-Type: text/event-stream using NLWeb event types (start, result, complete).

checks.name: REST response schema coverage
checks.details: 83% of operations define typed response schemas, 83% use application/json
checks.recommendation: Define typed JSON response schemas for every endpoint in your OpenAPI spec. Agents rely on these to know what fields they will get back; missing or partial schemas force trial-and-error.

checks.name: MCP tool annotations
checks.details: docs MCP: 4/4 tools have behavioral annotations
checks.recommendation: Add behavioral annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint) to your MCP tools. Agents use these to avoid destructive actions without user confirmation.

checks.name: MCP server-card.json
checks.details: MCP server card found at https://hashtagweb3.com/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json (4 tools advertised)
checks.recommendation: Publish a server card at /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json describing your MCP server. Required fields: name, description, version, serverUrl, tools[]. This lets agents preview your server before opening a transport connection.

checks.name: Product + docs MCP coverage
checks.details: You run an MCP server for your documentation, but not one for your product. This bonus needs two MCP servers: one for your product so agents can take actions, and a separate one for your documentation so agents can answer questions from your docs.
checks.recommendation: Beyond your product MCP server, expose a documentation MCP surface so agents can pull your docs and reference material over the same protocol they use to act. Covering both the 'do' and the 'learn' surfaces over MCP earns this.

checks.name: Sandbox / test environment
checks.details: Sandbox/test environment mentioned at https://hashtagweb3.com/auth.md but no sandbox surface verified
checks.recommendation: Provide a sandbox or test mode so agents can exercise your API without touching production data, and document how to reach it - this lowers the risk of a destructive call against live data.

checks.name: REST batch / bulk endpoint
checks.details: Batch endpoint found in OpenAPI spec (/batch path)
checks.recommendation: Offer a batch endpoint that accepts an array of operations in one request, documented in your spec, so an agent acting on many items can do it in bulk instead of looping one call at a time.

checks.name: MCP resources exposed
checks.details: MCP server exposes 7 resource(s) via resources/list
checks.recommendation: If your MCP server advertises the resources capability in its initialize handshake, make sure resources/list returns at least one resource. If you don't intend to expose resources, omit the capability - the check returns na with no penalty for tool-only servers. Quality of the resources you do return is scored separately by mcp-resource-quality.

checks.name: Agent-friendly 404s
checks.details: Nonexistent paths return a real HTTP 404. For full credit, include a short markdown body (site map links, where to look next) so agents can recover.
checks.recommendation: Return a real HTTP 404 (or 410) status for nonexistent paths - never a 200 with your app shell, which makes agents believe every path exists. For full credit, give the 404 response a short markdown body pointing agents at your sitemap, llms.txt, or docs index. Verify with `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://yourdomain.com/some-path-that-does-not-exist` - it must print 404.

checks.name: Accessible document structure
checks.details: Server HTML is a well-structured document (main=true, landmarks=4/4, h1=1, maxHeadingSkip=1).

checks.details: 80 native controls, 1 non-native div-soup affordances (99% native).

checks.name: Accessible names on controls
checks.details: 80/80 interactive elements have a computable accessible name (100%).

checks.details: 1/1 form controls have an associated label (100%).

checks.name: Accessibility-tree injection safety (bonus)
checks.details: No hidden instruction text detected in accessibility-tree attributes or off-screen content.

checks.name: MCP Apps support
checks.details: MCP Apps: 4 ui:// resources, 4 UI-enabled tools (search_jobs, search_glossary, get_news), correct MIME type
checks.recommendation: Add MCP Apps support to your MCP server using @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps. Expose ui:// resources and add _meta.ui.resourceUri to tools so agents can render interactive UIs directly in conversation.

checks.name: A2UI / generative UI support
checks.details: MCP Apps: 4 interactive ui:// resource(s) for in-conversation UI rendering
checks.recommendation: Support Agent-to-UI rendering via MCP Apps (ui:// resources), OpenAI Apps SDK, or generative UI patterns that let agents render interactive UIs in conversation.

checks.name: MCP Apps UI quality
checks.details: MCP Apps resource quality: correct MIME type, valid HTML5, dark mode support
checks.recommendation: Ensure your MCP Apps resources use MIME type text/html;profile=mcp-app, include <!DOCTYPE html>, and add <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark"> for dark mode. Never hardcode secrets in resource HTML.

checks.name: MCP App view reachable
checks.details: Inline ui:// view delivered with valid HTML and no auth wall
checks.recommendation: Make sure your MCP App view is reachable and public. For inline ui:// resources: return HTML with <!DOCTYPE html> and no login form. For external HTTP origins (referenced via <base href> or <meta refresh>): return 200 OK + text/html without requiring auth (no 401/403, no password input in the body).

checks.name: MCP App view CSP
checks.details: CSP covers all 4 categories: +connect-src covers MCP origin; +frame-ancestors covers ChatGPT and Claude.ai; +form-action / connect-src covers redirects; +asset directives are scoped
checks.recommendation: Add a Content-Security-Policy (via HTTP header or <meta http-equiv>) that scopes 4 directive categories: connect-src includes your MCP server origin; frame-ancestors includes both https://chatgpt.com and https://claude.ai; form-action (or connect-src) scopes redirect targets; img-src / script-src / style-src list specific origins (not *). Permissive default-src * receives partial credit but loses points compared to a properly-scoped policy.

checks.name: API schema complexity analysis
checks.details: REST: agent-friendly schema (12 operations, 100% with operationIds, 100% documented by description or summary)
checks.recommendation: Make your API spec self-describing: a unique operationId and a description on every operation, typed parameters, and response schemas. For GraphQL, a fully typed schema with a documented cost or rate limit reads best.

checks.name: Function calling compatibility
checks.details: Compatible: 12/12 ops with IDs, 12/12 with typed schemas
checks.recommendation: Ensure API endpoints have unique operation IDs, typed schemas, and descriptions compatible with LLM function-calling formats.

checks.name: MCP resource quality
checks.details: 7/7 resources read with valid mimeType and non-empty content
checks.recommendation: Ensure every resource returned by resources/list reads cleanly via resources/read: declare a valid mimeType, return non-empty content, and make sure any URIs in the content resolve. Broken or empty resources break agent UX silently.

checks.name: MPP payment protocol
checks.details: MPP documented (AI analysis: Streamable HTTP Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers); no live protocol surface found
checks.recommendation: Implement the Machine Payments Protocol so agents can pay for premium resources over HTTP 402. Return a complete WWW-Authenticate: Payment challenge - the full set of standard MPP parameters, not just the bare scheme - and advertise x-payment-info in your OpenAPI spec so agents can discover it.

checks.name: x402 payment protocol
checks.details: No commerce signals detected - agent-payment protocols are optional for non-commerce sites
checks.recommendation: Implement x402 payment protocol so AI agents can pay for API access via HTTP 402. x402 uses PAYMENT-REQUIRED/PAYMENT-SIGNATURE/PAYMENT-RESPONSE headers with Base64-encoded JSON. Add a /discovery/resources endpoint for agent discovery.

checks.name: UCP - Universal Commerce Protocol
checks.details: No commerce signals detected - agent-payment protocols are optional for non-commerce sites
checks.recommendation: Publish a UCP discovery profile at /.well-known/ucp with a required `version` (YYYY-MM-DD) and advertised `services`/`capabilities` per ucp.dev. Also expose the REST checkout surface (`POST /checkout-sessions` with `UCP-Agent` and `Idempotency-Key` headers) so agents can transact without per-vendor integrations.

checks.name: ACP - Agentic Commerce Protocol
checks.details: No commerce signals detected - agent-payment protocols are optional for non-commerce sites
checks.recommendation: Implement the Agentic Commerce Protocol checkout REST API: `POST /checkout_sessions` (create), update/get/complete/cancel variants, with `API-Version: YYYY-MM-DD` and `Idempotency-Key` required headers. Preflight OPTIONS should allow POST or return an ACP-shaped error with `supported_versions` so agents can negotiate.

checks.name: ACP delegate payment
checks.details: No commerce signals detected - agent-payment protocols are optional for non-commerce sites
checks.recommendation: Expose the ACP Delegate Payment endpoint at `POST /agentic_commerce/delegate_payment`. The request takes `payment_method`, `allowance` (max amount, currency, expiry, merchant scope), and `risk_signals`; the response returns a vault token. This lets agents pay on behalf of users with scoped, revocable credentials.

checks.name: AP2 - Agent Payments Protocol
checks.details: No commerce signals detected - agent-payment protocols are optional for non-commerce sites
checks.recommendation: Adopt Google's AP2 (Agent Payments Protocol) authorization layer: advertise an AP2 mandate capability (e.g. `dev.ucp.shopping.ap2_mandate`) in your UCP discovery profile, and verify the three signed mandates (Intent, Cart, Payment - SD-JWT verifiable digital credentials) server-side before routing to a settlement rail. Note: one agentic payment protocol is sufficient - AP2 is only needed if you are not already covered by x402 / MPP / ACP / UCP.

topFixes.name: Developer resource discoverability
topFixes.recommendation: Make your developer resources (API docs, OpenAPI spec, auth docs, developer portal, MCP server) discoverable by name. Publish them at predictable URLs, list them in llms.txt, and include your product name in page titles and headings so search engines surface them for name-based queries.

topFixes.name: Listed in MCP registries
topFixes.recommendation: Register your MCP server on Smithery (smithery.ai) or mcp.so so agent platforms can discover your tools. Link the registry entry from your homepage or docs for bi-directional verification.

topFixes.name: NPM/PyPI SDK package
topFixes.recommendation: Publish a JavaScript/TypeScript SDK package on npm so developers can integrate your API programmatically. In package.json set `repository` to your source repo and `homepage` to your product domain - these links are how agents confirm the package is your official SDK rather than a third-party tool with a similar name.

topFixes.name: Public API/docs linked from homepage
topFixes.recommendation: Publish API documentation at a discoverable URL (/docs, /api, /developers). Include authentication, endpoints, and example requests.

topFixes.name: Multi-language SDK packages
topFixes.recommendation: Publish official SDK packages across multiple language ecosystems (npm, PyPI, Go modules, RubyGems). Auto-generate them from your OpenAPI spec using tools like openapi-generator. For each package set the project URL or homepage to your product domain (package.json `repository`/`homepage`, PyPI `Home-Page` or `project_urls`, RubyGems `homepage_uri`) - this is how agents verify the package is your official SDK.

topFixes.name: Agent instruction / when-to-use
topFixes.recommendation: Tell agents when to reach for you: add a 'when to use this' section to your llms.txt (or a dedicated agent-instructions file) that names your best-fit use cases and how an agent should call you. Be specific about the jobs you are right for - generic marketing copy does not read as guidance.
